source.title: Quantifying the Capabilities of LLMs across Scale and Precision

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares downstream task scores across model sizes, using a different measure and setting from pretraining-loss scaling-law studies. It does not measure held-out pretraining loss or fit scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates zero-shot instruct models on downstream tasks and reports results by model size and precision. Those scores bear on V6. It does not test pretraining-loss power laws, extrapolation from smaller training runs, compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, architecture effects at fixed parameter count, or fit-dependence. Citations and descriptions of earlier scaling-law results are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study's own zero-shot results compare two sizes within each of two instruct model families across many downstream tasks. That bears directly on V6 (downstream performance improving with scale) in a new setting: post-trained chat models, small test samples and varied inference precision. It is a weak test. There are only two size points per family and no fitted trend. Mistral 7B vs Mixtral 8×7B is a sparse-MoE comparison, not a controlled parameter sweep. It measures no pretraining loss and tests none of V1–V5 or V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find a positive correlation between scale and performance on most tasks, but only marginal or no gains on analogical, deductive and some spatial reasoning tasks. Social-context misinformation detection depends less on scale, and Mistral 7B beats the larger models there. The record omits their second main conclusion: larger models are more resilient to quantization, so a 4-bit larger model is generally preferable to a smaller higher-precision model at similar memory.
record.recipe_differences: The original studies measure pretraining loss across parameter, data, and compute scales. This paper instead evaluates zero-shot downstream tasks on already trained instruct models and varies inference precision; it does not fit loss curves or compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Observed size trends differ by task and model family. The study also varies inference precision, though only FP16 results are retained here for several task comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger models lose less accuracy under 4-bit and 8-bit post-training quantization, and a 4-bit 70B model usually beats a 7B model at higher precision within a similar memory budget.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Robustness of downstream performance to inference-time quantization increases with model size.

record.problems: The authors note that limited sample sizes threaten external validity, evaluation is zero-shot, prompting may influence results, and selected metrics may not capture all aspects of capability. The comparisons involve instruct models and downstream scores rather than controlled pretraining runs; no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row cap is reached. Omitted separate results include other reasoning datasets and precision settings in Tables 5–6; other COVID-19 precision settings in Table 7; non-FP16 summarization settings in Table 8; other languages and precision settings in Table 9; and machine-translation results in Figures 6 and 8. The retained rows include multiple tasks and the principal reported reversals, ties, and positive size comparisons.

untested.parts: Predictability: no trend is fitted across more than two sizes, nothing is extrapolated, and downstream scores are not related to pretraining loss. The Mistral-family comparison mixes a dense model with a sparse MoE.
All of it: no pretraining loss is measured.

missing.what: Other FP16 reasoning size comparisons. Pep-3k reverses in the Mistral family (63.67 vs 50) and rises for Llama (43.33→70). Large Llama gains on CLUTRR (26.67→43.33) and e-CARE (43.33→70). bAbI-15 ties for Llama (46.67/46.67). StepGame basic is near-reversed for Llama (16.67→20). Also TimeDial, SpartQA basic, αNLI, CommonsenseQA and PIQA.
NusaX size comparisons in Javanese, Buginese and Indonesian. The 70B model beats the 7B in these, and Mixtral is mixed against Mistral.
Machine translation: the authors report larger-model gains bigger for low-resource than high-resource language pairs. Values appear only in figures.
The size gap depends on precision, e.g. the Llama TruthfulQA gap is about 6 points at 4/8-bit vs about 14 at FP16. This could be shown as a condition on V6.

record.verdict_notes: Each size comparison is entered twice (one row per model), which double-counts evidence. Sample sizes are 30–100 items per task, with no uncertainty reported, so differences of 1–2 items should not be weighted heavily. Mixtral 8×7B is a sparse MoE (about 47B total, about 13B active parameters) with different training from Mistral 7B, so the Mistral-family comparison is confounded. Neither original source is this study. The reader's MATH and EntailmentBank values were misread from Table 6, which flipped its MATH challenge label.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run loss from power laws fitted to smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss behavior beyond text pretraining, including other modalities and training regimes.
The study measures downstream task performance at several model sizes, but does not fit predictive relationships, test extrapolation, or relate downstream performance to pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices; bending of loss curves.

relationships.condition: Zero-shot instruct models, FP16/FP32 or quantized. Tasks: HotpotQA, MATH, StepGame basic-cardinal, TruthfulQA, COVID scientific, SAMSum (both families); SpartQA hard and CNN/DM (Llama family).
relationships.reason: The larger variant scores higher, often by 5–35 points (e.g. StepGame 60→95, 50→85; TruthfulQA 40.9→54.6; MATH 13.3→20, 30→50). Rows r01-r08, r11-r16, r25-r44, r51-r56.
relationships.display_finding: Larger variants often gained 5–35 points, including StepGame from 60 to 95 and 50 to 85, TruthfulQA from 40.9 to 54.6, and MATH from 13.3 to 20 and 30 to 50.

relationships.condition: EntailmentBank (both families), COVID social (Llama), Letter-String-Analogies (floor), and small reversals in the Mistral→Mixtral comparison on SpartQA hard, COVID social and CNN/DM
relationships.reason: Gains are marginal (one item) or absent at floor. The Mistral-family reversals are 1–3 points on 30–64 samples with no uncertainty reported. Rows r09, r10, r17-r24, r45-r50.
relationships.display_finding: Gains were as small as one item or absent at floor, while Mistral-to-Mixtral reversals were 1–3 points on 30–64 samples without reported uncertainty.

relationships.condition: NusaX English sentiment, FP16 (and identical at all precisions for Llama)
relationships.reason: The larger model scores lower in both families. Llama 2-Chat 70B drops to 0.649 from the 7B's 0.750, and the authors state this explicitly. Rows r57-r60.
relationships.display_finding: Both families scored lower at larger sizes, including Llama 2-Chat falling from 0.750 at 7B to 0.649 at 70B across all tested precisions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: HotpotQA, StepGame (basic-cardinal), TruthfulQA, COVID-19 scientific fact-checking, and SAMSum in the listed size comparisons
reader_labels.reason: Scores are higher for the larger variant in these comparisons; see r01-r04, r13-r16, r25-r40, r41-r44, and r53-r56.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope

reader_labels.reason: Some size comparisons are tied or go against the larger-is-better trend, while others favor the larger model; see r09-r12, r19-r20, r45-r48, and r49-r52.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: MATH, Letter-String-Analogies, and NusaX English at FP16
reader_labels.reason: Larger variants score lower in MATH for both families, lower on analogies for Mixtral, and lower on NusaX English for both families; Llama scores zero at both sizes on analogies. See r05-r08, r21-r24, and r57-r60.
